$comment: The file-system Survey Definitions (GovernanceActionProcess + chained steps) RE's Survey tab lists and executes for
the 'File System Directory' technology type — the file-system counterpart of ../survey-definitions-database/_batch.json.
A SEPARATE directory/batch, one per resource type, for the reason that file gives: bootstrap.py (BATCH_MANIFEST_FILE)
discovers batches one per directory, each with its own canary and post-heal reconciler.
Runs after questions (see ../_folder_order.json): each document's 'Link Element To Scope' commands bind the definition
to Question terms by name, and processing this batch while the questions batch is absent succeeds but creates no
ScopedBy link at all.
NOT IDEMPOTENT — see ../survey-definitions/_batch.json's own comment for the incident history: Dr.Egeria's 'Link
First/Next Process Step' commands do not dedupe. Only heal this batch when its canary is MISSING, and always run the
reconciler after a heal.
Canary is keyed on qualified_name: 'GovActionProcess::FilesystemAnalysisSurvey' is the larger of the two definitions
(7 steps) and its process element is created after all of its steps, so its presence means the document ran to
completion. It is listed last in `files` for the same reason. The two documents are otherwise self-contained.
Resource Explorer leads both definitions: every step is executes_at resource-explorer. Egeria's Folder Survey is not
part of them; where Egeria can read the folder it leads from the file system's folder-survey card, and the
definition's filesystem_inventory step refuses and says so.
Documents here are generated by ../../../scripts/generate_filesystem_survey_definition.py from
../filesystem_survey_types.csv — edit the CSV and regenerate, don't hand-edit the markdown.
REQUIRES engine-host (RE-HEAL-LEDGER-TRUST decision 4, 2026-11-07): this batch's 'Link Action to Action Executor'
blocks link its steps to ResourceExplorerSurvey, the engine the engine-host batch declares. Healed while that engine is
absent, every link fails and the definitions come back undispatchable. bootstrap heals this batch only once engine-host
is present in the same pass; otherwise it is reported blocked_by engine-host and nothing of it runs. The report-only
check scripts/reconcile_executor_links.py (post_heal_checks) says whether each step has exactly one.

post_heal.reason: Link First/Next Process Step are not idempotent; strip duplicate step edges a heal may have created.

post_heal_checks.reason: Report-only: ScopedBy links vs. each document's own 'Link Element To Scope' blocks. Never writes on this path — a heal must not silently remove or add scope links; it only surfaces drift for a person to act on.

Report-only: exactly one Link Action to Action Executor to ResourceExplorerSurvey per GovernanceActionType this batch's documents declare. Repairs only with --apply, which the engine-host batch's own post_heal passes, not this check.
